focus: P4 stale-worker successor safety proof and mutation-side fencing
noveltyJustification: The orientation identified a node-only completion hole; this iteration constructs the full stale-worker/successor counterexample, proves claim-time locking is insufficient, separates claim identity from monotonic mutation fencing, audits adjacent claim-derived mutation surfaces, maps the verified 036 prepare/revalidate/commit negative control, and defines the safe wave-admission boundary.
keyFindings: Graphene's documented revoked-claim completion refusal is contradicted by a done API that carries no claim identity or fence
After C1 expiry and C2 reclaim, stale done(node) sees C2's active-claim presence and can commit C1's output
GraphMutationCommandV1 must carry exact claim identity, current monotonic fence, expected version or head, and idempotent operation identity
Renew, release, checkpoint, completion, failure, retry, salvage, effect, and terminal mutations must never resolve caller ownership from node alone
036's prepare-without-side-effects then atomic current-fence revalidation and commit closes the exact stale-successor interleaving
Graphene read-set and claim admission can inform read-only lanes, but write-wave admission additionally requires a fresh authorized conflict-free plan and mutation-side fences
